short: Thomas Wolsey was a powerful Catholic cardinal and statesman who served as Henry VIII's almoner and Lord Chancellor.
full:
Rising from humble origins as a butcher's son in Ipswich, Thomas Wolsey became the most powerful man in England alongside the king. Henry VIII entrusted him with almost all matters of state and foreign policy. Appointed Archbishop of York and a cardinal in 1515, his immense wealth and ostentatious lifestyle made him deeply unpopular with the nobility, while his diplomatic maneuvering kept England influential in European affairs.

Wolsey's downfall was sudden and total, precipitated by his failure to secure papal annulment for Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon. Stripped of his government offices and properties, including Hampton Court, he was accused of treason in 1530. He died of natural causes at Leicester while travelling to London to face trial, avoiding probable execution and leaving the path clear for the English Reformation.
